# sysutils_ini_value (Resource)

Manages a single `key = value` setting inside a section of an INI-style file, such as a systemd drop-in, `php.ini`, a git config or `sshd_config`, without taking over the rest of the file, like Ansible's `ini_file`. Comments, ordering and unrelated content are kept; a missing section is created. Changes are written atomically and keep the file's mode and ownership.

Use it for configuration files that packages ship and other tools also edit, where [`sysutils_file`](./file.md) would take over the whole file and [`sysutils_file_line`](./file_line.md) doesn't know about sections.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Set a key in a section of php.ini, keeping every comment and other setting.
resource "sysutils_ini_value" "memory_limit" {
  path    = "/etc/php/8.2/fpm/php.ini"
  section = "PHP"
  key     = "memory_limit"
  value   = "512M"
}

# A systemd drop-in: the file and its [Service] section are created if needed.
resource "sysutils_ini_value" "app_restart" {
  path      = "/etc/systemd/system/app.service.d/restart.conf"
  section   = "Service"
  key       = "Restart"
  value     = "on-failure"
  separator = "="
  create    = true
}

# A git config subsection.
resource "sysutils_ini_value" "origin_url" {
  path    = "/srv/app/.git/config"
  section = "remote \"origin\""
  key     = "url"
  value   = "https://github.com/example/app.git"
}

# sshd_config has no sections and separates key and value with a space.
resource "sysutils_ini_value" "no_root_login" {
  path      = "/etc/ssh/sshd_config"
  key       = "PermitRootLogin"
  value     = "no"
  separator = " "
}

# Make sure a key is not set at all.
resource "sysutils_ini_value" "no_display_errors" {
  path    = "/etc/php/8.2/fpm/php.ini"
  section = "PHP"
  key     = "display_errors"
  state   = "absent"
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `key` (String) Name of the key. Compared exactly, including case. Must not contain the separator, and must not start with `#`, `;` or `[`. Changing this forces a new resource.
- `path` (String) Absolute path of the file to edit. Must be in canonical form (no `.`/`..` segments, duplicate or trailing slashes) and must not be `/`. A symlink at `path` is refused. Changing this forces a new resource.

### Optional

- `create` (Boolean) Create the file (mode `0644`, owned by the user running Terraform, missing parent directories with mode `0755`) if it does not exist. If `false`, a missing file is an error when `state` is `"present"`. Destroy never deletes the file. Defaults to `false`.
- `section` (String) Name of the section, as written between the brackets of its header, for example `Service` for `[Service]` or `remote "origin"` for a git config. Empty (the default) means the global section: keys before the first section header. Compared exactly, including case. Changing this forces a new resource.
- `separator` (String) Written between key and value. Its non-whitespace part is the delimiter used to split existing lines into key and value, for example `" = "`, `"="` or `": "`; if it is whitespace only (`" "`, as in `sshd_config`), the key ends at the first whitespace. Existing lines that already have the right value are not reformatted. Defaults to `" = "`.
- `state` (String) `"present"` to make `value` the key's only value, or `"absent"` to remove every occurrence of the key. Refreshed from the file, so a key that was added or removed outside Terraform shows up as a change of `state`. Defaults to `"present"`.
- `value` (String) Value of the key. Required when `state` is `"present"` and must not be set when it is `"absent"`. Written and compared literally, so quotes and trailing comments are part of the value. Must be a single line without leading or trailing whitespace; may be empty. If the key occurs more than once in the section, all its values are recorded, separated by line breaks, so the plan shows the duplicates.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) `path`, `section` and `key`, separated by colons. The value is left out, so that a secret in it is not shown in plans as part of the id.

## File Format

The file is read line by line:

- A line whose first non-blank character is `[` and that continues up to a `]`, optionally followed by a comment, is a section header. The section name is the text between the brackets without surrounding whitespace. Everything up to the next header belongs to that section. Lines before the first header belong to the global section (`section = ""`). A section whose header appears more than once is treated as one section.
- Lines whose first non-blank character is `#` or `;` are comments.
- Any other non-blank line is a key line. The key is the text before the first delimiter, the non-whitespace part of `separator` (`=` by default), and the value is everything after it, both without surrounding whitespace. If `separator` is whitespace only, the key ends at the first whitespace. A line without a delimiter is a key with an empty value, such as `skip-name-resolve` in `my.cnf`.

Values are compared literally. Quotes and trailing comments (`key = "x" ; note`) are part of the value, because their meaning differs between INI dialects. Keys and sections are compared exactly, including case, although some programs (such as git) ignore case. Line continuations and include directives are not interpreted. `sshd_config` `Match` blocks are not sections.

## Behavior

### `state = "present"`

- If the key exists in the section, its first occurrence is set to `value` in place, keeping its indentation, and every further occurrence in the section is removed. A line that already has the right value is left as it is, even if it uses a different separator style (for example `key=value` with the default `separator = " = "`).
- If the key does not exist, it is inserted right below the last commented-out occurrence of the key in the section (for example below `#PermitRootLogin yes`), otherwise below the section's last key line, with the same indentation, otherwise directly below the section header.
- A global key in a file with sections goes above the first section header and the comment lines directly above it, followed by a blank line. In a file without sections it goes at the end.
- If the section does not exist, it is appended to the end of the file, separated from the previous content by a blank line.

### `state = "absent"`

Every occurrence of the key in the section is removed. Comments, including commented-out occurrences of the key, and the section header are kept.

### Writing the file

- Nothing is written if the file already has the desired content, so the modification time only changes when content does.
- Everything except the lines of the managed key is kept byte for byte: comments, blank lines, ordering, indentation, other keys and sections, and line endings. Files with `\r\n` line endings are supported, and new lines get the line ending of the file's first line. A file without a line break at the end keeps not having one, unless a line has to be appended.
- Changes are written atomically, exactly as by [`sysutils_file_line`](./file_line.md#writing-the-file): the replacement gets the original file's owner, group, mode, ACLs and SELinux label before it is renamed into place, and the edit fails without writing if the file was changed by someone else in the meantime. Several `sysutils_ini_value` and `sysutils_file_line` resources editing the same file are serialised by the provider, so they can be applied in parallel safely.
- Files larger than 64 MiB are refused.

## Drift Detection

On refresh, the provider reads the file and looks up the key:

- If the value was changed outside Terraform, the actual value is recorded, and the plan shows an in-place update from it to `value`.
- If the key occurs more than once in the section, all its values are recorded, separated by line breaks (for example `"80\n8080"`). This never matches a configured value, so the plan shows that the duplicates will be removed.
- `state` is recorded as `"present"` or `"absent"` depending on whether the key is in the file. A key (or the whole file) removed outside Terraform therefore shows up as a change of `state` from `"absent"` to `"present"`, and a key added outside Terraform to a resource with `state = "absent"` as a change from `"present"` to `"absent"`.

Changes to `separator` or `create` alone don't rewrite a key that already has the right value.

## Destroy

With `state = "present"`, destroy removes every occurrence of the key from the section. The value it had before Terraform managed it is **not** restored, and the section header, the rest of the file, and a file created because of `create = true` are left in place. With `state = "absent"`, destroy does nothing.

## Import

An existing key can be imported with an ID made of the file's path, the section and the key, separated by colons. Use an empty section for global keys:

```shell
# <path>:<section>:<key>
terraform import sysutils_ini_value.memory_limit '/etc/php/8.2/fpm/php.ini:PHP:memory_limit'

# Global keys, before the first section header, have an empty section.
terraform import sysutils_ini_value.editorconfig_root '/srv/app/.editorconfig::root'
```

The path ends at the first colon and the key starts after the last one, so the section may contain colons (as in git's `[url "https://example.com/"]`), but paths and keys containing colons cannot be imported. The import ID has no separator, so the provider looks the key up with `separator = " = "`, then `": "`, then `" "`, and records the first one that finds it. A different `separator` in the configuration then causes an in-place update that doesn't change the file. If the key is not in the file, the import succeeds with `state = "absent"`.

## Caveats

- Consistent with the provider's [security model](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/blechschmidt/sysutils/latest/docs#security-model), a symlink at `path` is refused, and so is anything else that is not a regular file. Symlinks in the parent components of `path` are followed (inside the root if the provider's [`root_dir`](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/blechschmidt/sysutils/latest/docs#root-directory) is set). On destroy, a symlink or other non-regular file at `path` is left untouched, with a warning.
- The rename gives the file a new inode, which breaks hard links. If `path` is a mount point, the file is rewritten in place, which is not atomic. See [`sysutils_file_line`](./file_line.md#caveats) for details.
- Preserving an owner other than the user running Terraform requires the privileges to `chown` the replacement file, normally root.
- Two `sysutils_ini_value` resources for the same key, or a `sysutils_file` managing the same file, conflict with each other.
- Keys that legitimately occur more than once, such as git's `fetch` refspecs or systemd's `ExecStart=`, cannot be managed with this resource: it always leaves a single occurrence.
- The resource only works on Unix-like systems.
